title: Pronunciation Tips for Text-to-Speech Narration (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Fix Text-to-Speech Pronunciation in Your Script
slides.notes: Nothing breaks a training video like a narrator who says your company name wrong. The good news: the fix almost always lives in your script.

slides.title: Listen first, then list problem words
slides.notes: A voice reads exactly what's written and guesses at the rest. So listen to the whole narration first, and note every word that sounds off.

slides.title: Space out acronyms, spell names phonetically
bullets: After: the W H S portal
Siobhan becomes Shiv-awn in the notes
Correct spelling stays on the slide
slides.notes: If the voice reads WHS as a word, add spaces between the letters. For names, write them how they sound, and keep the real spelling on the slide.

slides.title: Write numbers the way people say them
slides.notes: Voices read numbers literally, so write them as people say them. Spell out symbols and units, and rephrase any word with two pronunciations.

slides.title: Fix rhythm and keep a team list
bullets: Shared list: WHS to W H S
slides.notes: Short sentences with clear full stops sound natural, not rushed. Keep one shared pronunciation list, so every deck your team makes sounds consistent.

slides.title: Clear narration, then an extraordinary video
bullets: Try Basic first, no subscription needed
slides.notes: Once your notes sound right, turn the deck into video. On Pro, a.i. directs it, landing each term as the voice says it. Start at powerpoint2vid.com.
